  "summary": "Replaces Bitcoin Core's private broadcast implementation with an isolated, node-stateless job engine and introduces a standalone bitcoin-privbcast CLI tool. Transaction broadcast targets are selected by resolving DNS seeds through Tor SOCKS5 proxies using dedicated circuits, and connections are established strictly over BIP324 v2 transport according to a pre-calculated random schedule. The PR removes legacy private broadcast peer connections and relay code from net and PeerManager, and extends the new engine to support 1-parent-1-child package relay via submitpackage.",

This creates observable timing oracles and fingerprinting vectors that an adversary can probe or manipulate via address gossip. In addition, the existing subsystem lacks package relay support, preventing private broadcast of low-fee transactions needing child-pays-for-parent to enter the mempool.",

result.summary: Replaces Bitcoin Core's private broadcast implementation with an isolated, node-stateless job engine and introduces a standalone bitcoin-privbcast CLI tool. Transaction broadcast targets are selected by resolving DNS seeds through Tor SOCKS5 proxies using dedicated circuits, and connections are established strictly over BIP324 v2 transport according to a pre-calculated random schedule. The PR removes legacy private broadcast peer connections and relay code from net and PeerManager, and extends the new engine to support 1-parent-1-child package relay via submitpackage.
result.problem: The existing in-tree private broadcast mechanism relies on node state (such as addrman, peer discouragement, and mempool arrival monitoring). This creates observable timing oracles and fingerprinting vectors that an adversary can probe or manipulate via address gossip. In addition, the existing subsystem lacks package relay support, preventing private broadcast of low-fee transactions needing child-pays-for-parent to enter the mempool.
evidence: PR description details historical privacy regressions and leaks from relying on node state, including a proxy bypass on v2-to-v1 retry (#35319/#35410), peer discouragement creating a clearnet oracle (#36312), mempool inspection leaking completion timing (#36277), and addrman state pollution (#35032)
PR description notes that drawing destinations from addrman allows remote peers to influence and fingerprint destination selection through address gossip
Commit ee5719d0c6 fixes a validation bug where two prioritisetransaction deltas near INT64_MIN caused a modified fee sum overflow in package handling
result.scope_notes: Very large multi-part change (+17k/-4.4k lines across 121 files) organized in four distinct sections: moving shared transport and BIP324 code into the common library, specifying and implementing the standalone bitcoin-privbcast tool, refactoring bitcoind -privatebroadcast into job queues while deleting legacy net/peerman broadcast logic, and adding 1P1C package validation and relay support. More than 11,000 lines are new unit, functional, and fuzz tests.
result.card: This PR completely replaces Bitcoin Core's private broadcast subsystem with an isolated, node-stateless job runner and introduces a standalone bitcoin-privbcast utility. The new design contacts DNS seeds over Tor to find IPv4/IPv6 peers and connects according to a predetermined randomized schedule over BIP324 v2 transport, eliminating reliance on internal node state and addrman. It removes the previous private broadcast peer connection and relay logic from net and PeerManager and adds 1-parent-1-child package relay support to submitpackage. The change is motivated by recurring privacy leaks in the legacy design, including direct proxy bypasses and clearnet peer discouragement oracles. It touches P2P networking, package validation, RPC, and CLI tooling across 121 files.

risk.why: Mistakes in the new SOCKS5 proxy state machine or BIP324 attempt loops could leak user IP addresses or fail transaction broadcasting entirely, while changes to package acceptance logic in validation could introduce mempool inconsistencies or crashes.
